review_type: Read-only source audit plus CPU unit tests and local cached pinned-tokenizer probes; LLM review, no human attestation

scope.source_identity_limit: These hashes bind audited local source. The already-completed remote worker/helper identity is not proved by this source-only audit.

main_conclusion: No confirmed assistant-EOT omission, incorrect label shift, or padding-loss leak was found in the inspected local loader/worker. A training-versus-evaluation mode-contract mismatch is confirmed. A microbatch-dependent loss-weighting property and missing worker/helper hash binding are confirmed. None establishes the cause of repetition or arithmetic regression without a controlled runtime check.

findings.claim: Assistant content plus exactly one 151645 EOT is loss-bearing; the trailing formatting newline remains in input but is masked.
findings.limit: The worker receives its tokenizer from Unsloth and imports a remote helper path; local checks do not prove those remote objects were byte-identical.

findings.claim: Offset-based assistant boundary avoids independently encoded-prefix BPE mismatch. Labels remain aligned to input positions and are passed directly to model; no manual label shift appears in worker. For three real pinned-tokenizer probes, shifted target count equaled loss-bearing label count and EOT remained a target.
findings.limit: The patched Unsloth model loss implementation was not inspected or executed; no claim of end-to-end runtime loss correctness is made.

findings.claim: Padding uses the pad ID for input, zero attention, and -100 labels; it cannot directly train on padding through these labels. Sequence overflow raises rather than truncates.
findings.limit: Worker pad_collate has no dedicated real-tensor test in its five-test suite, although the implementation matches the tested loader padding contract.

findings.claim: Training accepts only worked_solution and hint_level_1/2/3. Evaluation serializes fixture bookkeeping modes answer, hint_no_answer, student_error, and missing_or_contradictory_info as the model-facing mode without translating them. This changes a learned control field, although the natural-language problem and system prompt still explain the task.
findings.remediation: Keep frozen fixture IDs, semantics, original-mode provenance and original evaluation results. Add a separate contract-matched diagnostic: answer/student_error/missing_or_contradictory_info -> worked_solution; hint_no_answer -> a documented hint_level_1. Preserve user problem verbatim and the no-answer system constraint. Compare both prompts on the same untouched checkpoint before attributing benefit to retraining.
findings.causal_limit: Can explain out-of-distribution control routing; it has not been shown to cause the eight repeated outputs or the wrong arithmetic.

findings.claim: Each model-reported token-mean microbatch loss is weighted by example count. With unequal target lengths this differs from a global supervised-token mean, and changing microbatch partition from 1 to 2 can change gradient weighting. The config explicitly declares this objective, so it is not a hidden implementation mismatch.
findings.analytic_example: For two targets with 10 and 90 supervised tokens, microbatch=1 produces 0.5*mean_loss_10 + 0.5*mean_loss_90; one microbatch of 2 with token-mean loss gives 0.1*mean_loss_10 + 0.9*mean_loss_90. Equal-example and global-token objectives should be chosen deliberately.
findings.causal_limit: No evidence here establishes that this caused repetition or math regression. Changing it in a rescue run would be a new training variable.

findings.claim: Local cached official tokenizer reports eos_token_id=151645, matching the supervised assistant EOT; pad_token_id=151643. Generation passes tokenizer.eos_token_id. However decoded output skips special tokens and stores no raw generated IDs or terminal stop token, so old JSONL cannot rule out a runtime-specific stop-token mismatch directly.
findings.remediation: Before any bounded rescue training, assert actual Unsloth tokenizer eos_token_id and im_end ID equal 151645, run one CPU tokenization using the exact runtime helper, and record generated token count, final raw token ID, EOS/EOT occurrences and generation-config stopping IDs on the existing adapter. This is a diagnostic request, not an action performed by this audit.

findings.claim: The worker dynamically imports the helper from a configurable path; its saved config records data/fixture hashes but not helper/worker SHA256. Local correct code alone cannot establish the old remote helper identity.
findings.remediation: Record exact worker/helper source hashes and the runtime tokenizer metadata with the diagnostic and any rescue checkpoint.

tests.coverage_limit: Structural contract tests; tokenizer stub in manifest-binding test, no actual forward/loss/Unsloth model evaluation.

local_cached_tokenizer_probe.limit: Synthetic targets verify tokenization mechanics only. No model forward pass, GPU access, or additional generation was performed.

observed_failures.interpretation: Stopping or repetition controls alone cannot establish repair of these separate arithmetic failures.

next_diagnostic_order: Bind exact deployed worker/helper/tokenizer identity and assert EOT/labels/padding in that runtime before spending training compute.
Evaluate the existing checkpoint under original frozen prompts and separately logged contract-matched prompts, saving raw termination evidence.
Use untouched holdouts to distinguish prompt-contract improvement from arithmetic repair; preserve all original failures.

If a bounded rescue experiment is authorized, change only justified variables, keep the old checkpoint, and compare checkpoints using the frozen mathematical and hint-safety criteria. No rescue result or causal diagnosis is claimed by this audit.
